title: Uniform growth of a disc makes its daughter cells divide at different times

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Uniform growth of a disc makes its daughter cells divide at different times

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Uniform, symmetrical growth of a flattened disc does not imply uniform growth of its cells: after a quadrant divides into triangular and quadrilateral halves, the triangular cell gains area faster and reaches division size first (at about 1.345 times the radius, against about 1.517 for the quadrilateral).

fields.label: Notation
fields.value: after bisecting a quadrant: triangular cell reaches division size at 1.345r, quadrilateral at 1.517r

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. VIII: The Forms of Tissues, or Cell-Aggregates (continued)

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: For it shews us that a uniform and symmetrical growth of the organism (symmetrical, that is to say, under the limitations of a plane surface, or plane section) by no means involves a uniform or symmetrical growth of the individual cells, but may, under certain conditions, actually lead to inequality among these

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter VIII, “The Forms of Tissues, or Cell-Aggregates (continued)”; topic “Uniform growth and unequal cell division”. Scope: flattened discoid cell aggregates growing uniformly, such as Erythrotrichia

fields.label: Notation
fields.value: after bisecting a quadrant: triangular cell reaches division size at 1.345r, quadrilateral at 1.517r

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch08-06: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.60

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The ordering and numerical growth thresholds are sharply testable. Public time-lapse data may resolve individual examples, but datasets matching the idealized initial geometry and uniform growth assumption are sparse.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Track radial growth, daughter-cell area, and division timing after the asymmetric quadrant split and test the predicted ordering and radius ratios 1.345 versus 1.517.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Relevant long-term Erythrotrichia-like growth series are rare.

Uniform organismal radial growth must be verified independently.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The claim predicts both an order of division and two radius ratios under uniform disc growth. That is a clean test and it needs live, cell-resolved growth of that geometry. Such a series is not in current open datasets, so the constants cannot be confirmed or refuted without new observations.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Follow a uniformly growing flat disc after a quadrant divides into a triangular and a quadrilateral daughter, and record which daughter divides next and at what radius. The triangular cell reaching division size first, near 1.35 times the starting radius against about 1.52 for the quadrilateral, would support the claim; simultaneous division, or the quadrilateral dividing first, would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Fixed embryo collections cannot supply the division-time order this numerical prediction requires.

No public time-lapse of Erythrotrichia or a similar disc records daughter area against disc radius through the next division.
